title: Smith recognition from accessible weak equivalences
statement: Let $\mathcal A$ be a complete category with small Hom sets in a fixed universe. A category is locally presentable if it is cocomplete and, for some infinite regular cardinal $\kappa$, generated under small $\kappa$-filtered colimits by a small set of objects $P$ such that $\operatorname{Hom}(P,-)$ preserves these colimits. Here $\kappa$-filtered means every diagram with fewer than $\kappa$ morphisms admits a cocone, and regular means a union of fewer than $\kappa$ sets of cardinality less than $\kappa$ has cardinality less than $\kappa$. Suppose $\mathcal A$ is locally presentable. Let $C,W$ be classes of its arrows and write $\mathcal A^{[1]}$ for the category of arrows and commuting squares. Use diagonal lifting and arrow retracts as in [lem-coef-lifting-class-closure]. A weakly saturated class contains isomorphisms and is closed under pushouts, small transfinite compositions, and retracts in the arrow category; a small transfinite composition is the map from the first object to the colimit of an ordinal-indexed sequence continuous at limit ordinals. A full subcategory $\mathcal V\subseteq\mathcal D$ is an accessible subcategory if, for some infinite regular $\lambda$, it is closed under small $\lambda$-filtered colimits computed in $\mathcal D$ and is generated under those colimits by a small set of its objects. Assume (i) $C$ is weakly saturated and generated as such by a small subset, (ii) $C\cap W$ is weakly saturated, (iii) $W$ is an accessible full subcategory of $\mathcal A^{[1]}$, (iv) $W$ has two-out-of-three for composable arrows, and (v) every arrow with the right lifting property against $C$ lies in $W$. Then there is a combinatorial model structure, in the model-category sense of [lem-coef-simplicial-model-nerve-localization], whose cofibrations are $C$, weak equivalences are $W$, and fibrations are $(C\cap W)^{\square}$. In particular both weak factorization systems admit small generating sets and functorial factorizations. No simplicial enrichment or abelian-category assumption is made.

source.place: Proposition A.2.6.10, printed pp. 823-825 (PDF pp. 840-842), using Lemma A.2.6.9 for a small generating subset of C intersect W. Functoriality follows by the small-object argument for those sets. No Stacks tag states Smith recognition. Read online; not archived in literature/.

proof.text: Apply the small-generator lemma with the given $\mathcal A,C,W$. Its four hypotheses are precisely (i)–(iv), so choose a small $S\subseteq C\cap W$ whose weakly saturated closure is $C\cap W$. Also fix the small generating subset $C_0\subseteq C$ from (i). Put $F=(C\cap W)^\square$.

source.place: Lemma A.2.6.9, printed pp. 821–823; Proposition A.2.6.10, second factorization.

proof.text: For any small arrow set $I$, let $R=I^\square$. Every member of $I$ belongs to ${}^\square R$ by the lifting definition. Every isomorphism belongs to ${}^\square R$: for a square with left side $a$ invertible, the diagonal is $u a^{-1}$. The lifting-closure lemma gives pushout, composition and arrow-retract closure of ${}^\square R$, and the transfinite-left-lifting lemma gives closure under every small continuous transfinite composition. Thus the weak saturation $\operatorname{Sat}(I)$ is contained in ${}^\square R$. Consequently $I^\square=\operatorname{Sat}(I)^\square$: one inclusion is the preceding lifting argument and the other follows from $I\subseteq\operatorname{Sat}(I)$. In particular $C_0^\square=C^\square$ and $S^\square=F$.

source.place: Proposition A.2.6.10, printed pp. 823–824 (PDF pp. 841–842, numbered from 1).

proof.text: Completeness of $\mathcal A$ gives all small limits; cocompleteness in local presentability gives all small colimits. The weak saturation of $C\cap W$ also puts every isomorphism in $W$.

source.place: Proposition A.2.6.10, printed pp. 823–824 (PDF pp. 841–842, numbered from 1).

proof.text: Here is the retract argument for $W$, directly from its stated closure under sufficiently filtered colimits. Let an arrow $x$ be a retract of $y\in W$, with arrow-category maps $i:x\to y$ and $r:y\to x$ satisfying $ri=1_x$, and put $e=ir$. Choose an infinite regular $\lambda$ witnessing the filtered-colimit closure of $W$. The ordinal of all $\alpha<\lambda$ is small and $\lambda$-filtered: any fewer than $\lambda$ indices have an upper bound below $\lambda$ by regularity. On that ordinal take the diagram with every object $y$, all strict transition maps $e$, and identity self-maps. The equation $e^2=e$ makes it a functor. The constant cocone $r$ exhibits $x$ as its colimit: any cocone $(t_\alpha)$ has $t_\alpha=t_\beta e$ for $\alpha<\beta$; choosing a later index gives $t_\alpha e=t_\alpha$ and then all $t_\alpha$ are equal to a single $t$. Its unique factor through $r$ is $ti$, since $(ti)r=te=t$ and $ri=1_x$. Every vertex belongs to $W$, so its filtered-colimit closure puts a colimit object $x'$ of this diagram in $W$. If $x'$ is not $x$ itself, uniqueness of colimits gives an isomorphism $(a,b):x'\to x$ in $\mathcal A^{[1]}$, so $x=b\,x'\,a^{-1}$ with $a,b$ isomorphisms of $\mathcal A$. These lie in $W$ by step 3, and two-out-of-three (iv) applied twice puts $x$ in $W$. Thus no repleteness assumption is needed.

source.place: Proposition A.2.6.10, printed pp. 823–824 (PDF pp. 841–842, numbered from 1).

proof.text: Apply the accessible small-object factorization to $C_0$, whose smallness and locally presentable ambient category are among the hypotheses. Functorially factor every $f$ as $f=p i$ with $i\in\operatorname{Sat}(C_0)=C$ and $p\in C_0^\square=C^\square$ by step 2. Hypothesis (v) puts $p$ in $W$, and $C\cap W\subseteq C$ puts $p$ in $F$. Thus this is a functorial $(C,F\cap W)$ factorization.

source.place: Proposition A.2.6.10, printed pp. 823–824 (PDF pp. 841–842, numbered from 1).

proof.text: Apply the same small-object factorization to the small set $S$ from step 1. It functorially factors $f=q j$ with $j\in\operatorname{Sat}(S)=C\cap W$ and $q\in S^\square=F$, the last equality being step 2. This is the required functorial $(C\cap W,F)$ factorization.

source.place: Proposition A.2.6.10, printed pp. 823–824 (PDF pp. 841–842, numbered from 1).

proof.text: By the definition of $F$, every member of $C\cap W$ has the left lifting property against $F$. Conversely let $h:A\to B$ have that property and use step 6 to factor $h=qj$, with $j:A\to E$ in $C\cap W$ and $q:E\to B$ in $F$. Apply the lifting property to the square with top $j$ and bottom $1_B$ to obtain $d:B\to E$ with $dh=j$ and $qd=1_B$. The commuting squares $(1_A,d):h\to j$ and $(1_A,q):j\to h$ exhibit $h$ as an arrow retract of $j$. Weak saturation of $C\cap W$ therefore puts $h$ in that class. This proves ${}^\square F=C\cap W$.

source.place: Proposition A.2.6.10, printed pp. 823–824 (PDF pp. 841–842, numbered from 1).

proof.text: We first identify $F\cap W=C^\square$. The inclusion $C^\square\subseteq F\cap W$ was proved in step 5 using (v). For the converse take $p:X\to Z$ in $F\cap W$, and use step 5 to factor $p=r i$, with $i:X\to E$ in $C$ and $r:E\to Z$ in $C^\square\subseteq W$. Two-out-of-three for $p,r$ gives $i\in W$, hence $i\in C\cap W$. Since $p\in F$, the square with left $i$, right $p$, top $1_X$ and bottom $r$ has a diagonal $d:E\to X$ with $di=1_X$ and $pd=r$. The squares $(i,1_Z):p\to r$ and $(d,1_Z):r\to p$ exhibit $p$ as an arrow retract of $r$. Right lifting classes are closed under arrow retracts by the cited lemma, so $p\in C^\square$. Step 2 implies $C\subseteq{}^\square(C^\square)={}^\square(F\cap W)$. Conversely any $h$ in the latter left class factors as $h=r i$ by step 5; lifting $h$ against $r\in F\cap W$ gives, exactly as in step 7, an arrow retraction from $i$ onto $h$. Retract closure of $C$ gives $h\in C$. Thus $C={}^\square(F\cap W)$.

source.place: Proposition A.2.6.10, printed pp. 823–824 (PDF pp. 841–842, numbered from 1).

proof.text: Steps 5–8 establish the two functorial weak factorization systems required by the model-category definition in the cited node. Indeed the right classes are $C^\square=F\cap W$ and $(C\cap W)^\square=F$, and steps 7–8 identify their left classes. The class $C$ is retract closed by (i), $W$ by step 4, and $F$ by right-lifting closure. Together with the limits and colimits in step 3 and two-out-of-three (iv), these are all model-category axioms. Step 2 identifies the two right classes with $C_0^\square$ and $S^\square$, and steps 5–6 give their functorial small-object factorizations. Thus both weak factorization systems have the asserted small generating sets. Local presentability is assumed, so this is a combinatorial model structure with exactly the designated $C,W,F$; only the ordinary model-category definition from the cited node is used, with no simplicial hypothesis.

source.place: Proposition A.2.6.10, printed pp. 823–824 (PDF pp. 841–842, numbered from 1).

proof_origin.place: Proposition A.2.6.10 and Lemma A.2.6.9, read online (not archived). The proof follows that argument and explicitly supplies the generator-to-saturation lifting argument, filtered-colimit retract argument, and arrow-retract squares.
